Package neqsim.process.equipment.energy

Class CompressorPowerTrain

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.energy.CompressorPowerTrain
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class CompressorPowerTrain extends Object implements Serializable
Steady-state matching of a compressor shaft to a turbine or an electrical drive.

Reuses turbine site performance and motor/generator inverse conversion models. A gas-electric train has separate turbine and motor shafts: the compressor speed is passed only to the motor. Electrical auxiliaries are supplied upstream of the motor. Gearbox losses belong to CompressorShaft.setMechanicalEfficiency(double). Evaluating a train updates turbine fuel accounting, but does not change compressor duties or dispatch energy ports. Use CoupledProcessEnergySolver for a shared electrical network.

Catalogue turbine maps and default motor efficiencies remain screening assumptions. This adapter does not add gas-generator component matching, turbine output-speed maps, or rotor/control dynamics.

1.0

    • getTurbine

      public GasTurbineUnit getTurbine()
      Gets the turbine used for fuel and exhaust accounting.

      Returns the connected equipment itself. Configuration changes through this reference affect subsequent matching, and matching updates its fuel accounting. The train and its equipment must not be evaluated concurrently.

      Returns:
      live turbine, or null for an externally supplied motor

    • getAvailablePowerW

      public double getAvailablePowerW(double speedRpm, double ambientTemperatureK)
      Gets available compressor-driver output including every configured conversion limit.

      Bisection inverts the complete chain, including part-load efficiencies and idle losses. Inverse input power must increase with useful output over the configured range. No fuel calculation or energy-port dispatch is performed.

      Parameters:
      speedRpm - compressor driver speed in rpm
      ambientTemperatureK - turbine ambient temperature in K
      Returns:
      available mechanical output in W; infinity for an unbounded constant-efficiency electrical drive

    • evaluate

      public CompressorPowerTrain.Result evaluate(double requiredPowerW, double speedRpm, double ambientTemperatureK)
      Matches actual delivery to a requested mechanical duty and calculates fuel/electricity and losses.

      A shortfall is reported without overwriting the compressor's calculated pressure or duty. The caller must reduce throughput or re-solve speed before accepting that compressor point. Turbine minimum-load violations are reported separately: this method does not invent a dump load or a stable low-load combustion regime.

      Parameters:
      requiredPowerW - driver output required, including downstream gearbox losses, in W
      speedRpm - compressor driver speed in rpm
      ambientTemperatureK - turbine ambient temperature in K
      Returns:
      immutable operating point
